_comment: Per-army records in RAM. Base is the EWRAM pointer stored in ROM at
0x08282CBC; stride 0x68 comes from the damage path, which does
`movs r0,#0x68 ; muls r0,r6,r0` before indexing it.
The array is 1-INDEXED. Record 0 is a dummy and P1 is record 1. That is not
a guess: with P1 to move, record 1 held the on-screen funds at +00 while
records 2 and 3 held zero, and only the active player has spendable funds.
It also lines up with the terrain ownership encoding, where owner 0 is
neutral and 1..4 are the players -- so army record N owns tiles tagged N.
SUPERSEDED, and worth reading as a lesson: 'whoever holds funds is the
active player' was the only route to the current player, and it was an
INFERENCE from one capture. There is now a real field -- 0x03004424 holds
32 * player, 1-based -- so the reader uses that and keeps the funds rule
only as a cross-check. mgba_state.lua reports funds_heuristic_agrees on
every dump; if it ever goes false, the inference was wrong somewhere and
we find out at once instead of inheriting it.

provenance.method: live RAM capture, offsets pinned by on-screen values

0x00.name: funds_available
0x00.note: spendable now; zero for every player whose turn it is not

0x08.name: funds_incoming
0x08.note: income shown on the status screen; equal for all players here

0x20.name: co_power_meter
0x20.note: Charge, cumulative from 0. Confirmed by snapshotting the army records, attacking, and diffing: a single A-Air-on-Tank attack took P2 (attacker) 0 -> 3725 and P1 (defender) 0 -> 2900. Both sides charge, as AW does. The SCALE is unknown -- the activation threshold and the gain formula have not been worked out, and one attack is not enough to derive them.

0x1D.name: co_id
0x1D.note: The CO identity, 0..11. Indexes the CO record table as co*292 (see DERIVATION.md 11). WRITING IT CHANGES THE CO LIVE -- the name and portrait on the intel screen follow it -- which is how all eleven records were named without unlocking anything: 1 Andy, 2 Max, 3 Olaf, 4 Sami, 5 Grit, 6 Kanbei, 7 Sonja, 8 Eagle, 9 Drake, 10 Sturm, 11 Sturm. Record 0 untested. Constrain writes to 0..11; higher values index past a twelve-record table.

0x1E.name: co_statblock_index
0x1E.note: SOLVED, see DERIVATION.md section 11. Selects which 128-byte stat block within the CO's record applies -- almost certainly 0 = normal and 1 = CO power active. The full index read off 0x0803A734 is [0x08284A40 + weather*4 + [+0x1E]*128 + co*292]. The CO RECORD stride is 292, not 128; 128 is the sub-block stride, which is what the earlier reading got wrong. Observed as 0 for Andy, Max and Sami because no power was active in any of those captures.

open_questions.status: SOLVED -- see tools/extract_co.py and DERIVATION.md section 11. entry = [0x08284A40 + weather*4 + [army+0x1E]*128 + co*292]. The record stride is 292; the 128 assumed below is the SUB-BLOCK stride, and each record holds two sub-blocks (believed normal and CO-power-active). The modifier pointer array is indexed by the 1-BASED RAM unit type, the same off-by-one as the damage matrices, which is why an earlier read of it looked incoherent. Everything below is kept as the record of how it was wrong.
open_questions.question: How does the game select a CO's per-unit modifier record?
open_questions.detail: COs DO have passive modifiers -- Max's non-infantry direct-combat units have 150% firepower, and the ROM contains a record with exactly (150,100). So the reading below is incomplete, not a discovery that modifiers are absent.
open_questions.what_we_thought: The damage path computes its table index as unit_type*4 + [army+0x1E]*128, and +0x1E read 0 for Andy, Max and Sami alike, which would send every CO to record 0 (uniformly 100/100). That cannot be the whole mechanism.
likely_holes: +0x1E may be populated only while a battle is resolving, not between turns when we dumped it
the 0x08060Bxx path examined is the AI's damage ESTIMATOR; the live combat path at 0x08022Exx may differ in ways not yet read

the CO record base or 128-byte stride used by tools/co_mods.py may be wrong, in which case 'record 1 is Max' was never established -- its name pointer may simply point at the start of the CO name blob, which every record would share
CO stats appear to be MODE-DEPENDENT, so there is more than one record per CO -- see the sturm-duplicate note below
open_questions.why_it_matters: It justifies the neutral-CO requirement during calibration, which was kept and turned out to be correct.
open_questions.resolve_by: Dump the army records DURING a battle animation, and re-derive the CO record layout instead of assuming stride 0x80 from the first two entries.

progress.modifier_pool_found: The (attack, defence) pairs live in a shared POOL of 12-byte structs starting at 0x28491C, with attack at +5 and defence at +6. Observed pairs: (100,100), (120,90), (140,80), (150,100), (170,100), (90,110), (115,90), (80,100).
progress.significance: (150,100) is exactly Max's documented 150% firepower, so the mechanism is clear: a CO record holds one pointer per unit type, each selecting an entry from this pool. That is how a CO can be 150% on some unit types and 100% on others, and it explains why an earlier look found 'all pointers identical' -- that record simply was not Max's.
progress.still_wrong: The CO record layout itself. Assuming base 0x284B70 with stride 0x80, no record indexes the pool with a MIXED set of values, which cannot be right if any CO has selective bonuses. The base, the stride, or both are wrong.
progress.next_step: Find the CO records by searching for any 24-pointer run whose targets all fall inside the pool AND are not all identical. That locates real CO records without assuming a base or stride.

open_questions.status: CLOSED for 11 of 12. The CO name and portrait follow army +0x1D LIVE, so writing that byte and reading the intel screen binds a record directly -- no unlocking needed. Mapping: 1 Andy, 2 Max, 3 Olaf, 4 Sami, 5 Grit, 6 Kanbei, 7 Sonja, 8 Eagle, 9 Drake, 10 Sturm, 11 Sturm. Record 0 is untested; its luck bytes (10 normal, 50 under power) look like Nell, but that is a fingerprint and stays in 'untested'. The 'gap at 3' that made the ordering look non-contiguous was simply an unplayed CO: ids 1..11 run consecutively.
open_questions.question: What is the CO id ordering at +0x1D?
open_questions.detail: Three data points: Andy 1, Max 2, Sami 4. The gap at 3 rules out a simple select-screen ordering. P4 (Olaf) was not captured. Note also that the CO name blob at 0x2EA384 runs Max, Olaf, Sami, Grit, Kanbei, Sonja, Eagle, Drake, Sturm, Sturm -- an order that does not match these ids either, so the blob is probably a display list rather than an id table.
open_questions.resolve_by: armyhex(5) to reach record 4, plus a few more CO choices.

open_questions.status: ANSWERED. Records 10 and 11 BOTH report as Sturm on screen, and they are the only pair pointing their clear and rain movement slots at a table where every passable terrain costs 1. Predicted from the duplicate name in the CO blob before either was named. They differ at +11/+12 (130/120 vs 80/80), consistent with the mode-dependent stats described below.
open_questions.question: Why does the CO name blob contain 'Sturm' twice?
open_questions.detail: The blob at 0x2EA384 lists Sturm at both 0x2EA3C0 and 0x2EA3C8. Reported (unverified) behaviour is that Sturm's stats differ by mode -- 80/120 in VS, 130/80 in Campaign -- which two separate records would implement directly.
open_questions.implication: The CO table has MORE entries than there are COs, so any attempt to map index to CO by counting names or assuming one record each is unsound. It also means a modifier record is only meaningful together with the mode it belongs to.
open_questions.supporting_observation: An earlier survey of the table found records carrying (80,100) as well as (150,100) and (170,100), consistent with several distinct stat sets rather than one per CO.
open_questions.resolve_by: Compare the same CO's modifier record between a VS match and a Campaign mission.
